title: 12-Week Winter Arc
subtitle: Climbing, Strength & Physique
goals: Climb harder (finger strength, power, technique), get stronger and leaner, build visible abs, and improve aerobic fitness.
assumptions: Intermediate climber (roughly V3–V6 bouldering or 5.10–5.12 sport), at least 1 year of climbing, access to a climbing gym plus a weight room with a hangboard. Adjust grades and loads to your level.
effortScale: RPE 7 means about 3 reps left in the tank; RPE 9 means 1 left. Never train fingers to failure.

items.note: 5 min easy cardio · band pull-aparts + external rotations ×15 each · wrist and finger circles · 10–15 easy problems building from 3 grades below max to 1 below.

phases.name: Foundation
phases.focus: Volume, technique, base strength, tendon prep
phases.guidance: Build volume, movement quality and tendon resilience at moderate loads. Add a little weight or a rep each week in weeks 1–3.
phases.lastWeekNote: Deload week: cut every set count by about 40%.

items.name: Hangboard repeaters
items.note: 20 mm edge, open-hand or half-crimp. Bodyweight or feet-assisted so it feels RPE 6. 3 min between sets.

items.name: Bouldering volume
items.note: 1–2 grades below your max, 3 min rest. Precise footwork, quiet feet.

items.name: Technique drill
items.note: Silent feet, hover hands, or flagging on easy terrain.

items.name: Single-leg RDL
items.note: Square hips, slow lowering. Builds hip stability for high steps.

items.name: Cossack squat
items.note: Bodyweight or light goblet. Hip and ankle mobility for heel hooks and wide stances.

items.name: Zone 2

items.name: Pull-ups

items.name: Push-ups or dips
items.note: Push work balances all the pulling and protects your shoulders.

items.name: Reverse wrist curls + finger extensor band
Zone 2
items.note: Low-impact choices spare your legs. Winter option: hike, snowshoe or cross-country ski.

items.name: 4×4s
items.note: 4 problems 3–4 grades below max, climbed back-to-back. Rest 4 min between rounds.

items.name: Continuous traversing or auto-belay laps
items.note: Easy terrain. Aerobic capacity for forearms.

phases.name: Build
phases.guidance: Heavier loads and lower reps for strength, with extra hypertrophy volume for physique. Add 5–10 lb to a main lift whenever you complete every rep at RPE 8 or below.
phases.lastWeekNote: Deload week: cut every set count by about 40%.

items.name: Max hangs
items.note: 20 mm edge, half-crimp. Add weight (belt or vest) so each hang feels like you could do 13 s. Increase 2–5 lb per week.

items.name: Limit bouldering

cardio.intro: About 80% of cardio is easy Zone 2 for recovery and aerobic base; about 20% is short, hard intervals.
cardio.zone2: Zone 2 means you can hold a full conversation but not sing (roughly 60–70% of max heart rate). Use an incline walk, bike, rower or easy jog. Low-impact choices spare your legs before Tuesday squats.
cardio.warning: Keep at least one true rest day. If your resting heart rate is up 5+ bpm for several mornings, drop that week's intervals.

guide.title: Weekly rules
items: Hard climbing days never fall back-to-back. Leg day sits between them so your fingers get 48 hours off.
Can only do 4 days? Keep Mon, Wed, Fri, Sat. Fold Tuesday's squats and deadlifts into Saturday and do cardio on two rest days.
Weeks 4 and 8 are deloads. Take them seriously, even if you feel great.

guide.title: Core & abs
items: Core A (Mon, Fri, after climbing, 15 min) builds climbing-specific tension. Core B (Wed, after upper body, 15 min) is loaded ab growth.
Add load or difficulty when you hit the top of the rep range with clean form.
Visible abs come from building the muscle here and keeping body fat in check through nutrition.

guide.title: Recovery
items: Sleep 7–9 hours a night, with consistent bed and wake times.
10 min of mobility after each session: hips, thoracic spine, lats, chest and forearms.
Finger tendons adapt more slowly than muscle. Sleep, protein and smart load management decide most of your results.

guide.title: Nutrition
items: Protein: about 0.7–1 g per lb of body weight daily, spread over 3–5 meals.
For a leaner look, run a small deficit (about 300–500 kcal/day) and lose no more than ~0.5% of body weight per week so strength keeps climbing. For more size, eat at maintenance or a small surplus.
Fuel climbing and lifting days well; hard sessions suffer on empty.
Drink to pale-yellow urine. Winter means less sun, so consider having vitamin D levels checked.

guide.title: Finger & shoulder care
items: Stop any hang or climb at the first sharp pain in a finger or pulley. Never push through it.
Prefer half-crimp and open-hand grips; limit full crimping on small holds.
Do antagonist work (push-ups, extensor bands, face pulls) every week.
Sharp, persistent pain or a pop in a finger means rest and see a physio or sports doctor before training again.
